videos.caption: The Silent Echo, 2021 Suman Sen (writer director) @sumansen In Mustang - one of the remotest districts of Nepal - childhood is often threatened by “loss, migration, and vanishing certainties.” Here, geography dictates destiny. When confronted by this harsh landscape, what do children dream of? What brings them joy, and how far do they travel for it? ‘The Silent Echo’ is director Suman Sen’s attempt to “listen to children growing up in a landscape where nature is both guardian and threat.” The film follows the journey of four young friends from Mustang who are determined to navigate the practical obstacles to achieve one big dream - winning a band competition in a distant town. Despite the bleak conditions, the children share inner worlds which remain tender and playful. #nepal #girlhood

A massive debris-laden flash flood struck the Budhi Gandaki River in Gorkha's Chumnubri Rural Municipality after a landslide blocked the river flow. Viral footage captured the shocking moment a giant boulder rolled relentlessly down the grey torrent, highlighting the severe destruction caused by the sudden surge. The flash flood swept away more than 35 houses, several bridges, and local infrastructure across riverside settlements like Jagat and surrounding areas. While authorities have reported no human casualties so far, hundreds of residents have been displaced as rescue teams and security forces mobilize to assess the heavy damage. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) and local administration have issued urgent high-risk alerts. Residents along the Budhi Gandaki and Trishuli river corridors have been strictly advised to move away from riverbanks and stay on high ground. 🚨Shocking visuals coming from Nepal's Gorkha District today. A massive, black debris-filled flood surged down the Budhi Gandaki River early this morning after a landslide blocked the river in Chumnubri village. The temporary dam suddenly burst, unleashing a wall of water, mud and rocks. In the video you can see entire buildings with green roofs being swallowed in seconds as people watch helplessly from the hilltop. According to authorities, more than 35-65 houses in Salleri Bazaar, Jagat, Paiyuka and riverbed settlements have been swept away. At least 4 bridges including 2 motorable bridges were destroyed. 5 to 10 people are reported missing so far, and 49 people have been rescued and airlifted by the Nepal Army. A RED ALERT has been issued for downstream districts - Gorkha, Tanahun, Chitwan, Nawalparasi. Residents are being urged to stay away from the river and move to high ground. This comes just 2 months after the deadly August flood in Nepal that killed over 1,400 people. Pray for Nepal. 🙏 #NepalFlood #PrayForNepal #Gorkha #FlashFlood #NepalNews
